as_told.title: The Space Act lets NASA withhold sensitive findings

plain: The law that created NASA, the National Aeronautics and Space Act passed by Congress in 1958, is said on the show to bind NASA closely to the Pentagon and to let it keep certain findings secret. If so, NASA's public, civilian face would not be the whole story. A researcher named Maaneli Derakhshani makes the first point without naming a source. He calls it "just the observation" that NASA and the Department of Defense "have always been very tightly linked in law" through the act that created NASA. Michels goes further in his own framing. He says some matters fell "outside the civilian mandate", so that if NASA found anything strategically sensitive, such as "a breakthrough in propulsion, a powerful new sensor, or even contact with non-human intelligence" (the field's term for minds that are not human), "it could be withheld indefinitely." So two people tell it: a researcher describes the legal link, and the host spells out what he thinks it allowed NASA to hide.
